rounds.text: Redington presents a compelling valuation gap, trading at a P/E of 14.2 and a price of Rs 327 despite a discounted cash flow model suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 678 [E1, E44]. This 51.8% margin of safety is underscored by the fact that the market price implies only 6.0% earnings growth, even though the company achieved a 42% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E45, E46, E21]. The company’s operational efficiency is elite, with an ROCE of 18.4% and an ROA of 4.45% that far exceeds the sector benchmark of 3.05% [E12, E8]. Growth momentum is intensifying, evidenced by a 35% year-over-year increase in sales and a 94% surge in net profit [E60, E62]. Foreign institutional investors have recognized this potential, raising their ownership to 63.42% as part of a broader positive money flow [E41, E43]. Financial health remains robust with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x and a consistent dividend payout of 34.8% [E37, E58]. Conceded: The company’s cash conversion is currently low at 0.18x, and its P/E of 18.54x sits slightly above the sector benchmark of 17.61x [E34, E6].

Redington trades at a valuation premium relative to its sector, evidenced by a P/E of 18.54x against a benchmark of 17.61x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 11.39x compared to the sector average of 10.27x [E11]. The quality of these earnings is undermined by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.18x, which indicates that reported profits are significantly ahead of actual cash generation [E34]. Operational stability is further questioned by inconsistent operating-margin trends over both the last year and the last two quarters [E32] [E33], within a business model flagged as cyclical [E57]. While recent profit growth appears strong, the three-year compounded profit growth is a much lower 5% [E20], borrowings have increased to Rs 2,842 Cr [E39], and domestic institutions have reduced their holdings to 16.01% [E42]. The stock carries substantial risk for investors, highlighted by annualised volatility of 42.7% [E53] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2% [E52]. Conceded: The company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E37] and has seen trailing twelve-month sales growth of 23% [E17].

While the bear cites a valuation premium [E6, E11], filed statements show a lower P/E of 14.2x [E1], and any premium is earned by a ROCE of 18.4% [E12] that is more than double the sector median of 7.1% [E68]. Conceded: cash conversion is currently low at 0.18x [E34], yet the business generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr [E35] and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E36]. Despite inconsistent margins [E32, E33] and cyclicality [E57], the bear’s focus on stagnant 3-year profit growth [E20] overlooks the recent 42% trailing twelve-month profit growth [E21]—well above the sector median of 17.2% [E66]—and a 94% year-over-year net profit increase [E62]. Although borrowings rose slightly [E39], the company remains conservatively financed with a 0.28x debt-to-equity ratio [E37] while aggressively investing in growth, evidenced by a 400% increase in capital work-in-progress [E40]. Furthermore, the reduction in domestic holdings [E42] is outweighed by foreign institutions increasing their stake to 63.42% [E41], contributing to overall positive money flow [E43]. Finally, historical volatility [E53] and drawdowns [E52] are mitigated by a 51.8% margin of safety relative to intrinsic value [E45], a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E50], and a high-confidence screen score of 95 out of 100 [E59].

Conceded: [E1] and [E12]. The bull asserts that a P/E of 14.2x [E1] and an ROCE of 18.4% [E12] justify valuation premiums, but this ignores independent data provider metrics showing higher trailing valuation multiples of 18.54x P/E [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 11.39x [E11] sitting above sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. Conceded: [E35] and [E36]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 231 Cr [E35] and free cash flow hit Rs 125 Cr [E36], the severe cash conversion ratio of 0.18x reveals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection, pointing directly to hidden risks in receivables and accruals [E34]. The bull leans heavily on recent TTM profit growth of 42% [E21] and a 94% year-over-year net profit spike [E62], yet completely sidesteps the persistent reality of inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margins [E32, E33] alongside a stagnant 3-year profit growth rate of just 5% [E20]. Although the bull cites a 400% surge in capital work-in-progress [E40], this capex build-up phase coincides with rising total borrowings of Rs 2,842 Cr [E39] and a thin current ratio buffer of 1.41x [E38]. Finally, the reliance on a foreign institutional holding of 63.42% [E41] glosses over the simultaneous exodus of domestic institutions trimming their stake to 16.01% [E42], while ignoring the staggering historical vulnerability of an 80.2% peak-to-trough drawdown [E52] paired with high annualised volatility of 42.7% [E53].

The bear questions the valuation, but the company trades at a modest P/E of 14.2x [E1] alongside a strong ROCE of 18.4% [E12], which handily beats the broader sector median ROCE of 7.1% [E68]. Conceded: [E34]. While cash conversion reads 0.18x for Mar 2026, the business still generated tangible operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36]. The bear dismisses profit momentum because of a prior 3-year growth rate, ignoring the powerful acceleration seen in a 42% TTM profit surge and a rules-based screen scoring 95 out of 100 with high confidence [E21, E59]. The capital expenditure reflected in the 400% surge in CWIP is safely backed by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.28x [E37, E40]. Finally, foreign institutional ownership has expanded significantly to 63.42%, accompanied by positive institutional money flow, demonstrating robust backing where it matters most [E41, E43].

Conceded: [E12]. While ROCE outpaces the sector median, the bull's reliance on a modest P/E of 14.2x [E1] ignores that key ratios peg the P/E higher at 18.54x, which actually trades at a premium to the sector benchmark of 17.61x [E6]. Furthermore, the bull downplays the dismal cash conversion of 0.18x for Mar 2026 by citing absolute cash flow figures [E34, E35, E36], yet a 0.18x ratio explicitly warns that profits are running far ahead of actual cash and requires checking receivables and accruals [E34]. The bull also defends the 400% surge in CWIP using the conservative debt-to-equity ratio [E37, E40], but omits that total borrowings actually increased to Rs 2,842 Cr from Rs 2,809 Cr a year earlier during this heavy capital expenditure phase [E39]. Conceded: [E41]. Although foreign institutional holdings have expanded, domestic institutional ownership has simultaneously declined to 16.01% from 17.92%, showing institutional divergence rather than unanimous backing [E42]. Finally, the high confidence screen and recent profit spikes [E21, E59] mask a volatile underlying operating history, evidenced by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2% [E32, E33, E52].
